text: The Sales Director agreed to a definition: active means a purchase in the trailing ninety days, churned means none in ninety-plus days but two or more purchases in the prior year. That sounds settled, but it hasn't met real data yet.

Profile the data before writing the final query. A quick diagnostic groups customers by how many purchases they made in the last twelve months, zero, exactly one, or two-plus. That single query surfaces every edge case worth a ruling.

Four rulings get added as an addendum, not a rewrite. One-time buyers stay excluded, since they were never retained. Returns and refunds with a net total at or below zero don't reset the purchase clock. Holiday-only shoppers who buy in the same six-week window every year get flagged Seasonal, not folded into churned. And wholesale accounts are out of scope entirely.
Each ruling gets the same five-minute confirmation email as the original definition, because an unapproved exception is just as risky as an unapproved assumption.
The definition is now stress-tested against real behavior. Next: deciding which tool, Power BI, Tableau, or Excel, serves which audience.
